London, 9<sup>th</sup> January 2009 



# Norilsk Nickel Daily News Digest 

**J.D. Power** cut its 2009 western European auto market forecast by 600,000 units on Wednesday following a bleak December sales month and now sees volumes down 16% for the full year to levels last seen in 1993.  The automotive forecasting arm of J.D. Power expects sales of just 11.39 million vehicles in western Europe.  Double-digit declines are expected in Italy, while Spain will contract by 25 percent and Germany will slide to just 2.75 million units, “a level not seen since the 1980s,” the forecaster said. 

The UK car market is seen plunging “well below” 1.7 million units after 2.13 million in 2008.  Only France could see relatively decent demand with J.D. Power anticipating the year would be “somewhat tougher.” The forecast for western Europe comes on top of an 8.4 % slide last year to 13.56 million new cars.  The last time the market shrank to its forecast 2009 level was in 1993, said European sales forecast manager Jonathon Poskitt. Between 2005 and 2007, sales stagnated around 14.7 million. _Source:  Reuters_ 

**Johnson Matthey’s** latest generation diesel particulate filter has been verified by the US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and the California Air Resources Board (CARB).  The Continuously Regenerating Technology (CRT(R)) filter is produced by JM’s Emission Control Technologies department.  The filter - which can reduce PM, HC and CO emissions by over 85%- meets the EPA and the CARB’s tough NO2 slip requirement, while it is also the first to be verified by the EPA’s voluntary refit programme. _Source:  Johnson Matthey_ 

**Ridge Mining,** which is scheduled to start commissioning its flagship Blue Ridge platinum mine later this month, has agreed to defer payments due for three projects that it is selling to Bushveld Platinum, but, in return, has negotiated a higher price.  In light of the current financial difficulties, Ridge has agreed with Bushveld that, instead of paying R13-million when the transaction closes, Bushveld will instead pay R16-million on December 31 09.  If the R16-million is not paid in time, it will increase to R20-million, and if Bushveld lists on any stock exchange before the end of the year, it also can opt to settle the purchase price in shares worth R20-million at the listing price.   “This deferral and option to settle in shares enables Bushveld to concentrate its cash resources on fulfilling its obligation to keep the prospecting licences on the projects in good standing prior to ministerial consent to the transfer,” Ridge said. _Source:  Mining Weekly_ 

**Impala Platinum** confirmed that a worker at its No 14 shaft, in Rustenburg, died.  The Department of Minerals and Energy (DME) conducted an inspection and issued a Section 54 notice.  The shaft will remain closed until the DME and Implats meet to decide on what further steps need to be taken. _Source:  Mining Weekly_ 

**The DME** confirmed this week that the number o

f workers that lost their lives in South Africa’s mining industry fell in 2008.  However, the DME’s inspector of mines, Thabo Gazi did not give a concrete number; the department is finalising its statistics to be released by the end of January.  Trade union Solidarity in December reported that 168 workers had died in mining accidents in 2008, a 23% decline on the 221 workers who died in 2007. 

_Source:  Mining Weekly_
